title: Rottermund Krzysztof
name: Rottermund Krzysztof
description: music historian and theorist; b. 25th August 1957 in Kalisz. He attended the Henryk Melcer Primary and Secondary State Music School in Kalisz (Instrumental Department: violin) and the Technical School of Piano Building, where he was a student of the outstanding pianist Gustaw Arnold Fibiger. In 1983 he graduated with honours in music theory from the Karol Lipiński Academy of Music in Wrocław. In 1992 he obtained his doctorate under the supervision of prof. Ludwik Bielawski at the Institute of Art of the Polish Academy of Sciences in Warsaw, in 2006 he received his habilitation from the University of Wrocław. From 1983 he worked as an assistant and senior assistant at the Higher Teacher’s School in Kielce (now Jan Kochanowski University), and in 2000-2010 as an assistant and then associate professor at the University of Szczecin. In 2010-2012 he was a professor at the Academy of Art in Szczecin. Since the 2012/13 academic year he is a professor at the Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Faculty of Pedagogy and Art in Kalisz. He worked as a piano tuner, also dealing with the restoration of historic keyboard chordophones. He prepared a number of record cards of historic musical instruments for the National Heritage Board of Poland (formerly the National Centre for Research and Documentation of Monuments). He collaborated with the Museum of Industrial History in Opatówek (elected to the Museum Council for the 2016-2020 term). He was also an expert at the Ministry of Culture and Arts in the field of pianos. He received two rector's awards (1986, 2007), twice received a scholarship from the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage (2006, 2007), and in 2010 he was awarded the medal of the University of Szczecin 'Sis qui es – pro publico bono'. He took an active part in over fifty conferences, symposia and scientific sessions, including the 3rd International Chopin Congress in Warsaw (2010) and events at the University of Bonn (2004, 2008), the University of Leipzig (2008), the National University of Ireland, Maynooth (2012) and the German Historical Institute in Moscow (2013). In foreign libraries and archives he found a number of unknown works, autographs and manuscripts related to Polish musical culture. He edited and published two volumes of ‘Studia Musicologica Stetinensis’, published three books, many encyclopedic entries and scientific and popular science articles, reviews, reports, etc., also abroad (Berlin, Chemnitz, Laaber, Leipzig, Messel, Stuttgart, Los Angeles, New York).
